zh.title: 紐西蘭 TAIC 公布 Q300 低於安全高度事件報告　提出兩項新建議
zh.summary: 報告指出機組監控、飛航管理系統操作、訓練與監管均為促成因素；事件未造成傷亡或飛機損壞。
body: 紐西蘭運輸事故調查委員會（TAIC）於 2026 年 10 月 1 日公布 AO-2023-007 最終報告。2023 年 6 月 13 日，Air New Zealand 一架註冊編號 ZK-NEM 的 De Havilland Canada DHC-8-311（Q300）夜間進場 Timaru 時，偏離預設下降剖面約 2,500 呎，並在最低安全高度為 2,000 呎的區域下降至最低 1,156 呎。機上有 33 名乘客及 3 名機組員，航機其後恢復高度並正常落地，無人受傷，飛機亦未受損。
TAIC 認定，機組為調整高度表設定而把下降模式切換至垂直速度模式後，未重新選回原定模式；兩名駕駛又專注尋找機場（TIU）燈光，導致儀表掃描與飛行路徑監控不足。報告也指出機組資源管理、Air New Zealand 的訓練與 Q300 機隊安全管理，以及紐西蘭民航局對航空公司的監督均有缺失。
TAIC 提出兩項新建議：Air New Zealand 應繼續與 De Havilland Canada 尋求技術方案，使飛航管理系統在轉換高度時可計算平順下降剖面；紐西蘭民航局則應透過國際民航組織適當論壇，推動把延長座艙語音紀錄器錄音時間的要求擴及現行須裝設紀錄器的運輸類飛機。

en.title: New Zealand TAIC issues final report on Q300 descent below safe altitude
en.summary: The report identifies flight-path monitoring, avionics procedures, training and regulatory oversight as factors and makes two new recommendations.
body: New Zealand's Transport Accident Investigation Commission published its final report AO-2023-007 on October 1, 2026. On June 13, 2023, Air New Zealand De Havilland Canada DHC-8-311 ZK-NEM descended about 2,500 feet below its programmed profile during a night approach to Timaru and reached 1,156 feet in an area with a minimum safe altitude of 2,000 feet. The aircraft, carrying 33 passengers and three crew, regained altitude and landed without injury or damage.

TAIC found that the crew changed from the intended descent mode to vertical-speed mode while adjusting altimeter settings and did not reselect the planned mode. Both pilots then became focused on locating the aerodrome lights, degrading instrument scanning and flight-path monitoring. The report also identified issues involving crew resource management, Air New Zealand's training and Q300 safety management, and the Civil Aviation Authority's oversight of the airline.

TAIC made two new recommendations. Air New Zealand should continue working with De Havilland Canada on a technical solution that allows the flight management system to calculate a smooth descent through transition altitude. The Civil Aviation Authority should also promote, through an appropriate ICAO forum, wider extended-duration cockpit voice recorder requirements for transport aircraft that are already required to carry a recorder.

operators: Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand

facts.claim: TAIC published final report AO-2023-007 on 2026-10-01 about Air New Zealand Q300 ZK-NEM descending below minimum safe altitude near Timaru on 2023-06-13.
The aircraft descended about 2,500 feet below its programmed profile and reached 1,156 feet in an area with a 2,000-foot minimum safe altitude.
There were 33 passengers and three crew aboard, and the flight landed without injury or aircraft damage.
TAIC identified flight-mode selection, task fixation, ineffective crew resource management, training and regulatory oversight factors.
TAIC issued two new recommendations covering a technical flight-management-system solution and wider extended-duration cockpit voice recorder requirements.
